rationale: Expression is fully explicit and solvable for v (no derivatives/integrals per analyze_expression), so equation_type=explicit / integrator=evaluate_explicit. v is the dependent variable; I (inhibitor concentration) is the only physical sampling axis and the phenomenon is an inhibitor sweep, so it gets the range. I range [0,100] spans well beyond Ki and Kii so both competitive and uncompetitive channels are exercised. The new gamma (ESI residual-activity) term is the difference from the parent; excitation_check confirms it reaches ~21.7x the sigma=1 noise, strongest at high I, so it leaves a clear mark in the data.

scenario_text: A reversible inhibitor is titrated into an enzyme assay while substrate is held at a fixed concentration. As inhibitor concentration increases, the apparent catalytic velocity declines because the inhibitor competes for the active site. Velocity is measured across an inhibitor sweep. The task is to describe how velocity depends on inhibitor concentration.
